name: Raise the Bar
definition: We set ambitious goals, build high-performing teams, and deliver feedback that pushes everyone to grow.

rows.situation: When the target is being set
rows.under: Sets what last year plus a little would produce.
rows.justRight: Sets what would be genuinely ambitious, then works out what has to change to reach it.
rows.over: Sets a number nobody believes, and the team stops treating targets as real.

rows.situation: When the feedback would be uncomfortable
rows.under: Gives the general, positive version, and nothing changes.
rows.justRight: Gives the specific version, with the behavior, the effect, and what you want instead.
rows.over: Gives so much corrective feedback that the person stops taking any risk.

rows.under: Accepts it, to avoid the conversation.
rows.justRight: Says what would make it good, and expects the next version to get there.
rows.over: Sends work back over details that change nothing for anyone.

rows.situation: When the team is not strong enough
rows.under: Works around the weak spots for years.
rows.justRight: Fixes it, by developing the person or by changing the team, and starts now.
rows.over: Churns the team so often that nothing institutional survives.

rows.situation: When the bar applies to you
rows.under: Holds others to a standard you do not meet.
rows.justRight: Holds your own work to it first, and visibly, so the standard is credible.
rows.over: Reworks your own output endlessly, and becomes the thing the team waits on.
